column3: Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text in naming “those who followed” (οἱ) separately; “the disciples” supplies a subject for “they.”
Close to the Greek.
Close to the Greek.
BSB supplies “Jesus” for the pronoun and renders the present “come” as past; the Greek explicitly says “the two sons.”
“Inquired” renders the Greek “said.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB’s future “I will drink” and “I will undergo” render the Greek present “I drink” and “I am baptized.”
“The brothers” makes the Greek pronoun explicit.
“These seats belong” supplies an explanatory clause where the Greek says only “but for whom it has been prepared.”
The Greek says they “began” to be indignant.
“Said” renders the Greek present “says.”
BSB’s “shall not be” matches the future of the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the present “is not” (ἐστιν). “Must be” renders “will be.”
The Greek says “will be” rather than “must be,” and explicitly includes “among you.”
Close to the Greek.
“Next” and “named” are supplied; the Greek uses present “come” and refers to Jesus by a pronoun.

The Greek explicitly asks what He should “do” and says “said” rather than “asked.”
BSB’s “followed Jesus” matches the Textus Receptus (Ἰησοῦ); the critical text has “Him” (αὐτῷ). “Healed” renders “saved.”
